C-ESTABLISH-OPENWEARSYNC-BASELINE.Summary: Establish the approved, verifiable product and technical baseline for OpenWearSync, a Wear OS to Windows voice-recording transfer system over local Wi-Fi.
C-ESTABLISH-OPENWEARSYNC-BASELINE.Problem: Syncthing-Fork sustained background network activity on Galaxy Watch and caused unacceptable battery drain even when the Windows computer was unavailable. OpenWearSync currently has a GRACE 4 bootstrap but no product-specific contracts, modules, or verification projection.

Goals.Goal: Provide one-way, lossless transfer of large Samsung Voice Recorder files from Galaxy Watch to a Windows PC over local Wi-Fi, including a Samsung phone hotspot.

Specify the target architecture without temporary rewrite stages: shared Rust transfer core on watch and Windows; Kotlin platform integration and Compose for Wear OS; Rust receiver and Kotlin Compose Desktop UI.
Define idempotent, resumable, authenticated, encrypted sessions with durable receiver checkpoints and no automatic deletion of source recordings.
Define energy-bounded behavior: no persistent watch discovery engine, no unbounded retry loops, and resource cleanup on completion, cancellation, timeout, or failure.
Establish normative GRACE context, current graph ownership, matching verification contracts, project layout, and measurable release gates in a subsequent approved execution.

Constraints.Constraint: Target devices are Samsung Galaxy Watch with Wear OS and a Windows PC; Galaxy S25 Ultra Wi-Fi hotspot is a required network topology, not a data-processing intermediary.
Files move over Wi-Fi, not Bluetooth; no cloud server or mandatory phone companion application.
Rust handles portable protocol, chunking, hashing, transfer state, and Windows receive/server logic. Kotlin owns Android lifecycle, permissions, user interface, Wi-Fi selection, and energy policy.
Long-running user-initiated transfers must use supported Wear OS foreground or job facilities; automatic operation must be OS-cooperative, bounded, and opt-in.
Do not assume that ADB shell visibility proves third-party app file access; verify Samsung recording reads without elevated privileges on real hardware.
Do not assume Samsung hotspot allows station-to-station traffic or multicast discovery; demonstrate watch-to-PC connectivity and provide a manual endpoint fallback when routing is possible.
No product implementation, durable graph/verification projection updates, or approved plan may be written while this change remains a draft specification.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Syncthing protocol compatibility or generic peer-to-peer bidirectional directory synchronization.
Bluetooth transport for recording payloads, external hosting, mobile-data relay, or compulsory Samsung phone application.
Uploading still-growing recordings, transcoding audio, transcription, or deleting originals by default.
Creating throwaway intermediate implementations before the approved target architecture is built.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A versioned baseline defines boundaries for watch shell, Android platform adapter, shared Rust core, discovery, authentication, receiver, storage registry, desktop UI, and energy policy, with explicit interfaces and ownership.

Requirements establish exactly-once durable file outcome under reconnect, receiver restart, duplicate delivery, corrupt chunks, and interrupted transfers, without claiming network exactly-once delivery.
Security contracts cover authenticated pairing, encrypted transfer, pinned receiver identity, path traversal prevention, and bounded resource consumption.
Energy contracts specify idle behavior, event and timeout ownership, retry ceilings, cleanup paths, and on-device comparative battery tests.
Product contracts include Samsung recording file access tests, hotspot station-to-station connectivity tests, Wi-Fi network binding tests, and fallback to saved/manual server address.
Proposed context files, module graph and one-to-one verification entries will be created through a subsequent approved GraceChangePlan, with lint and review evidence.
The proposed baseline distinguishes confirmed decisions from unverified physical-platform assumptions and assigns acceptance gates to those assumptions.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Draft GRACE artifacts parse and satisfy GRACE 4 grammar; approval is separate from validation.

After approval and implementation: Rust unit and integration tests, Kotlin and JNI tests, Windows build, Android/Wear OS device tests, hotspot routing tests, interrupted-transfer tests, and comparative battery/thermal measurements.

Assumptions.Assumption: Recording storage is conventionally visible at /sdcard/Recordings/Voice Recorder/ via ADB; app-level access must be demonstrated separately.
Watch and PC connect as Wi-Fi clients to the S25 Ultra hotspot; direct client traffic and multicast discovery remain unverified.

Release targets, minimum Wear OS/Android versions, precise pairing UX, distribution method, and numerical performance thresholds remain to be validated and finalized without weakening security or energy requirements.
Automatic synchronization does not require waking immediately upon each file-system change; bounded user-invoked and scheduled sessions are acceptable.
